title: Who was in Russell's early Nest band, and the unhealthy club
summary: He recalls early tenor players (one dangerous, one named Adams), local drummers, and Pops Foster and Barbarin coming from Chicago, and the airless club.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, Higgenbotham... He wasn't there when I went there, but...
Do you remember who was there on trombone when you got there?
Hmm...when I went in Russell's band there was no trombone. There was no trombone. He had a tenor... myself, a tenor and a trumpet. I think it was Edward Anderson on trumpet.
No. The tenor player...he was a fellow from St. Louis. I don't know if I can think of his name right now. Kind of wild. He was the kind you didn't play

He would! He was a nice guy, but he didn't play. You know, he was one of them kinds you don't play with. But he'd shoot you in a minute. But he was a nice guy. I can't think of his name. He was a small guy.

And then, while I was there at the same time, what's his name, Dude... Not Dude Adams? Adams, a tenor player... Do you remember Adams? He was a big guy; a big, round(?) guy. And he used to play tenor and pound his feet, and he looked real terrible sitting up there on the bandstand. His name was Adams, but what his first name was I don't know. He could blow loud and look ugly and (?). He stayed a while...
Who replaced George Howe? Did Barbarin come in to replace Howe?

Well, no, he didn't replace George Howe at the time, because... I mean, he was just using local drummers from around. And then he got the idea of sending to Chicago, trying to get these men he had with'..these men that worked with King Oliver. See, that's when Barbarin... The first one was Pops Foster. He got Pops Foster first. And then Paul Barbarin. And I think... When I went out the band, I think Simeon came in to take my place. Because I

was leaving for some other job, going somewhere else.
I mean, there was never no scarcity of musicians. He could always get somebody. Of course, that was no...that place was not conducive to good health down there. It was a little bitty place, and no air coming in and no air going out, and it would be packed full of people. I mean, you worked there a while and then you taken off, so you could get your lungs back together again.
